title: Introduction to Tajweed
description: Understanding the definition, purpose, and legal ruling of learning Tajweed.

lessons.title: Definition of Tajweed
lessons.definition:
Linguistically, Tajweed means 'improvement' or 'to make something better'.

Terminologically, it means: 'Giving every letter its rights and dues from its articulation point.'

'Rights of the letter' (Haqq al-Huruf) refers to its permanent characteristics that never change, such as Al-Jahr, Isti'la', and Istifal.

'Dues of the letter' (Mustahakk al-Huruf) refers to temporary characteristics that appear in certain conditions, such as Tafkhim (heavy), Tarqiq (light), and Ikhfa'.

lessons.title: Ruling on Learning Tajweed
lessons.definition:
The theoretical knowledge of Tajweed rules is Fardhu Kifayah (Communal Obligation) – meaning if some members of the community learn it, the obligation is lifted from the rest.

However, reading the Quran with proper Tajweed application is Fardhu 'Ain (Individual Obligation) for every Muslim.

It is possible for a reciter to read correctly without knowing the technical terms (like Idzhar or Mad). But for those who cannot read correctly, it is mandatory to strive to improve their recitation to meet the standard set by the Prophet Muhammad Sholallohu'alaihi wasallam.

title: Nun Sakinah & Tanween
description: Rules applied when Nun Sakinah (نْ) or Tanween (ـً ـٍ ـٌ) meets specific Hijaiyah letters.

lessons.title: Idzhar Halqi
lessons.definition: Idzhar linguistically means 'clear'. In Tajweed, it means pronouncing the Nun Sakinah or Tanween clearly without Ghunnah (nasalization) when followed by one of the Throat Letters (Halqiyah).

lessons.title: Idgham
lessons.definition: Idgham linguistically means 'to merge'. In Tajweed, it is the merging of Nun Sakinah or Tanween into the following letter. It is divided into Idgham Bighunnah (with nasal sound) and Idgham Bilaghunnah (without nasal sound).
lessons.note: Divided into Bighunnah (With Ghunnah) and Bilaghunnah (Without Ghunnah)

lessons.title: Iqlab
lessons.definition: Iqlab linguistically means 'to change'. In Tajweed, it is changing the sound of Nun Sakinah or Tanween into a 'Mim' when followed by the letter Ba, accompanied by Ghunnah.

lessons.title: Ikhfa Haqiqi
lessons.definition: Ikhfa linguistically means 'to hide'. In Tajweed, it is pronouncing the Nun Sakinah or Tanween in a state between Idzhar and Idgham, without Tasydid, and with Ghunnah.

title: Mim Sakinah
description: Rules when Mim Sakinah (Mim with Sukun) meets other Hijaiyah letters.

lessons.title: Ikhfa Syafawi
lessons.definition: Ikhfa Syafawi occurs when Mim Sakinah meets the letter Ba. The pronunciation of Mim is hidden/concealed with Ghunnah.

lessons.title: Idgham Mimi
lessons.definition: Idgham Mimi (or Mitslain) occurs when Mim Sakinah meets another Mim. It must be pronounced with Ghunnah.

lessons.title: Idzhar Syafawi
lessons.definition: Idzhar Syafawi occurs when Mim Sakinah meets any letter other than Mim and Ba. The Mim must be pronounced clearly without Ghunnah, especially when meeting Fa and Waw.

title: Qalqalah Rules
description: Rules for echoing/bouncing the sound of Qalqalah letters (ب ج د ط ق) when they are Sakinah (silent) or Waqaf (stop).

lessons.title: Qalqalah Kubra (Major)
lessons.definition: Qalqalah Kubra occurs when a Qalqalah letter is silenced due to stopping (Waqaf) at the end of an Ayah or word. It should be pronounced with a strong and clear echo.

lessons.title: Qalqalah Sugra (Minor)
lessons.definition: Qalqalah Sugra occurs when a Qalqalah letter has an original Sukun (not due to stopping) and is in the middle of a word. It should be pronounced with a light echo.

title: Lam & Ra Rules
description: Rules for thickening (Tafkhim) and thinning (Tarqiq) the pronunciation of Lam (in Allah's name) and the letter Ra.

lessons.title: Lam Jalalah (The Name of Allah)
lessons.definition:
Tafkhim (Heavy): Pronounced heavily (like 'Aw') if preceded by Fathah or Dhommah.
Tarqiq (Light): Pronounced lightly (like 'La') if preceded by Kasrah.

lessons.title: Ra Rules
lessons.definition:
Tafkhim (Heavy): Ra with Fathah/Dhommah, or Sukun preceded by Fathah/Dhommah.
Tarqiq (Light): Ra with Kasrah, or Sukun preceded by Kasrah.

title: Mad Rules (Prolongation)
description: Rules for prolonging the sound of Mad letters (Alif, Waw, Ya).

lessons.title: Mad Thabi'i (Natural)
lessons.definition: Mad Thabi'i occurs when Alif is preceded by Fathah, Ya Sukun by Kasrah, or Waw Sukun by Dhommah. Elongated for 2 beats.

lessons.title: Mad Wajib Muttashil
lessons.definition: Mad Thabi'i followed by a Hamzah within the same word. Must be elongated for 4-5 beats.

lessons.title: Mad Jaiz Munfashil
lessons.definition: Mad Thabi'i followed by a Hamzah (in the form of Alif) in the next word. Elongated for 4-5 beats.

lessons.title: Mad Badal
lessons.definition: Hamzah preceding a Mad letter within the same word. Elongated for 2 beats.

lessons.title: Mad 'Aridh Lissukun
lessons.definition: Mad Thabi'i followed by a letter that becomes silent due to stopping (Waqaf). Elongated for 2, 4, or 6 beats.

lessons.title: Mad Lin (Soft)
lessons.definition: Waw or Ya with Sukun preceded by Fathah, followed by a letter silenced by stopping (Waqaf). Elongated for 2, 4, or 6 beats.

lessons.title: Mad 'Iwadh (Compensation)
lessons.definition: Stopping at a letter with Fathah Tanwin (an) at the end of a sentence. Elongated for 2 beats.

lessons.title: Mad Lazim Muthaqqal Kilmi
lessons.definition: Mad followed by a Shaddah (double letter) in the same word. Must be elongated for 6 beats.

lessons.title: Mad Shilah (Ha Pronoun)
lessons.definition: The Pronoun Ha (Hu/Hi) located between two moving vowels. Divided into Qashirah (Short-2 beats) if not followed by Hamzah, and Kubra (Long-4/5 beats) if followed by Hamzah.

title: Mad Lazim
description: Mad that must be elongated for 6 beats (Harakah) due to meeting Sukun or Shaddah.

lessons.title: Mad Lazim Muthaqqal Kilmi
lessons.definition: Occurs when Mad Thabi'i meets a letter with Shaddah (doubled) within one word. It is read heavily and elongated for 6 beats.

lessons.title: Mad Lazim Mukhaffaf Kilmi
lessons.definition: Occurs when Mad Thabi'i meets a letter with original Sukun within one word. It is read lightly and elongated for 6 beats. It only appears twice in the Quran (Surah Yunus).

lessons.title: Mad Lazim Muthaqqal Harfi
lessons.definition: Occurs in the opening letters (Muqatta'at) spelt with 3 letters, where the middle is Mad and the last is merged (Idgham) into the next. Elongated for 6 beats.

lessons.title: Mad Lazim Mukhaffaf Harfi
lessons.definition: Occurs in the opening letters (Muqatta'at) spelt with 3 letters, where the middle is Mad and the last is Sukun (silent) without merging. Elongated for 6 beats.

title: Other Mad Rules
description: Special Mad rules like Mad Farq and Mad Tamkin.

lessons.title: Mad Farq
lessons.definition: Mad used to distinguish between a question (Istifham) and a statement. It occurs when Question Hamzah meets a definite article. Elongated for 6 beats.

lessons.title: Mad Tamkin
lessons.definition: Occurs when a Ya with Kasrah and Shaddah meets a Ya with Sukun. It is read for 2 beats with emphasis (Tamkin) on the Shaddah.

title: Muqatta'at Letters (Opening)
description: Rules for reading the opening letters (Fawatihus Suwar) of Surahs.

lessons.title: Mad Thabi'i Harfi (Hayyun Thahura)
lessons.definition: Opening letters spelt with 2 letters (Ha, Ya, Tha, Ha, Ra). Elongated for 2 beats.

lessons.title: Special Case of 'Ain
lessons.definition: The letter 'Ain in the opening of Surah Maryam and Asy-Syura. Can be read for 4 or 6 beats (6 is preferred). Called Mad Lin Lazim.

title: Gharaib Readings (Special)
description: Special readings outside general Tajweed rules.

lessons.title: Saktah (Pausing)
lessons.definition: Pausing briefly without taking a breath for about 2 harakats, then continuing.

lessons.title: Isymam (Gesturing)
lessons.definition:
Gesturing a hidden Dhommah by puckering the lips without producing sound, while holding the Ghunnah in 'Laa Ta'manna'.

How to Read:
1. Read 'Laa Ta'man...' (hold the Ghunnah on the double Nun).
2. While holding the hum, pucker your lips (gesturing Dhommah) without changing the 'Nnn' sound.
3. Pull lips back to finish the Fatha (na).

lessons.title: Imalah (Inclination)
lessons.definition:
Inclining the Fatha sound towards Kasra (like the 'a' in 'name' or 'e' in 'bed'). Only one instance in Quran (Majreeha).

How to Read:
In the word 'Majraaha', the letter Ra is read thinly (Tarqiq) with an 'e' vowel sound (like 'Ray'). It is pronounced 'Majreeha'.

lessons.title: Tashil (Softening)
lessons.definition:
Pronouncing the second Hamzah softly (between Hamzah and Alif). It sounds like 'A-ah-jamiyyun'.

How to Read:
1. The first Hamzah (A) is read clearly.
2. The second Hamzah is read softly/vaguely, sounding like a mix of 'ah' and 'a'.
3. It sounds like: 'A-ah-jamiyyun'.

lessons.title: Naql (Transfer)
lessons.definition:
Transferring the vowel of the Hamzah to the preceding silent letter (Sukun). 'Bi'sal-ismu' becomes 'Bi'salismu'.

How to Read:
1. The Alif (Hamzah Washal) in 'Al-Ismu' is silent.
2. The Kasrah (i) from the Hamzah of 'Ismu' is transferred to the previous Lam (Al).
3. It becomes: 'Bi'salismu'.

title: Other Idgham Rules
description: Rules for merging letters based on origin and characteristics.

lessons.title: Idgham Mutamatsilain
lessons.definition:
Meeting of two letters that are EXACTLY the same in makhraj and characteristics. The first letter is silent (sukun), the second is voweled.

How to Read:
Merge the first letter into the second (like a tasydid).

lessons.title: Idgham Mutajanisain
lessons.definition:
Meeting of two letters that share the SAME makhraj but have DIFFERENT characteristics.

How to Read:
Merge the first letter into the second.

lessons.title: Idgham Mutaqaribain
lessons.definition:
Meeting of two letters that are CLOSE in makhraj and characteristics.

How to Read:
Merge the first letter into the second.

title: Alif Lam Rules
description: Rules for reading 'Al' (The) when meeting other letters.

lessons.title: Alif Lam Syamsiyah
lessons.definition:
Alif Lam is MERGED (silent) into the following letter.

How to Read:
Connect directly to the next letter with emphasis (tasydid).

lessons.title: Alif Lam Qamariyah
lessons.definition:
Alif Lam is read CLEARLY.

How to Read:
Pronounce the Lam clearly.

title: Waqaf Signs
description: Guide to stopping while reading Quran.

lessons.title: Waqaf Lazim (Mim)
lessons.definition:
MUST Stop.

Meaning:
Complete meaning. Continuing might spoil the meaning.

lessons.title: Waqaf Mamnu' (Lam Alif)
lessons.definition:
FORBIDDEN to Stop.

Meaning:
Incomplete meaning. Must continue.

lessons.title: Waqaf Jaiz (Jim)
lessons.definition: Allowed to Stop, Allowed to Continue.

lessons.title: Waqaf Mu'anaqah
lessons.definition: Stop at ONE of the three-dot signs.
